assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy is a bench-to-bedside arc of very high originality and enormous clinical impact: gut-hormone biology, the glucose-dependent insulin response and appetite effects, and durable agonist drugs transforming diabetes and obesity care.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and the active GLP-1 forms), Drucker (preclinical/translational biology) and Mojsov (peptide chemistry, early characterization) are plausible core contributors; Knudsen's industrial drug-design role is important but is the fourth name and credit among the peptide-chemistry contributors is contested.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy is established at large scale through multiple independent trials and approvals; the underlying physiology is well replicated. Recognition is timely and arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Mojsov, Habener, Holst, Drucker and industrial chemists is unresolved and partly contested.
Long-term safety profile of chronic therapy is still maturing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors created a new class of living drugs, producing durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies; conceptually original and clearly impactful.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June drove CAR design (costimulatory domains) and clinical translation; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T-cell trials. Earlier receptor-design work (Eshhar) is not in the credited names, a limitation of the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent confirmation in leukemia and lymphoma; extension to solid tumors and toxicity management remain open, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Credit for the founding chimeric-receptor concept falls partly outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response is a conceptually clean discovery of ER-to-nucleus signaling (Ire1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing), opening a field of proteostasis relevant to diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori separately defined the Ire1 pathway and the transcriptional output; the pairing is compact and well supported by the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism has been confirmed for decades in yeast and mammals and is textbook; translational relevance (e.g., integrated stress response modulators) still developing, but fundamental maturity is high.
uncertainties: Whether additional contributors (e.g., Kaufman, Ron, Schekman lineage) are expected is not resolved within the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics transformed causal neuroscience, enabling cell-type-specific control of activity with light; the tool is extraordinarily widely adopted and the discovery of channelrhodopsin is original and clear.
assessment.attribution: Nagel, Bamberg and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsin; Boyden, Deisseroth and Miesenboeck made the neuronal implementation and earlier genetic photo-control concepts. A three-person prize must exclude several well-supported people.
assessment.maturity: Broadly confirmed across thousands of labs, with emerging clinical use in vision restoration; recognition is mature.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among six credited people is difficult and contentious.
The prize-relevant balance between photoreceptor discovery and neuronal application is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense splice-switching of SMN2 produced nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy and a landmark for RNA therapeutics; mechanism and clinical benefit are unusually clear.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and target elements; Bennett led the antisense chemistry and drug development. The two-person configuration is coherent.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with strong independent clinical confirmation; long-term outcomes and its role alongside gene therapy continue to be studied.
uncertainties: Contributions of other groups to SMN2 splicing and ASO chemistry could be raised.
Commercial development makes discovery versus development credit complex.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR identification and the nutrient/growth control pathway are a foundational cell-signaling discovery with implications for metabolism, aging, cancer and immunosuppression.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically; Schreiber's work on rapamycin and FKBP12-rapamycin target biochemistry is decisive. Sabatini's mTOR contributions are credited but I would be cautious about including him given allocation questions.
assessment.maturity: Pathway well confirmed and clinically used (rapalogs); some downstream interpretations still evolving.
uncertainties: Allocation among Hall, Schreiber, Sabatini and the mammalian mTOR discoverers is uncertain; I have not independently verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defines how cytosolic DNA is sensed to trigger innate immunity, with strong relevance to autoimmunity, infection and cancer immunotherapy.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the second messenger cGAMP; Barber identified STING. Other credited names are important but this pairing carries the decisive discoveries.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is robustly confirmed; therapeutic translation (STING agonists/inhibitors) is not yet realized, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Priority of STING discovery among multiple groups is not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL11A as a fetal-hemoglobin repressor, from human genetics to enhancer editing, led to an approved gene-editing therapy for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia.
assessment.attribution: Orkin and Sankaran defined BCL11A's role; Bauer contributed the erythroid enhancer editing strategy; Thein's GWAS-related genetic work is also credited. Selecting three is plausible but contestable.
assessment.maturity: Approved therapy in 2023 with early durable results; long-term follow-up is limited, so this may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Long-term safety and durability data are limited.
Attribution among genetic-association and editing contributors is unsettled.
